topic.name: The Coordinates of a Vector Relative to a Basis in Abstract Vector Spaces

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 6 \\ -3 & 3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 9 \\ -6 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 8 \\ -5 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 6 \\ -3 & 3 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 9 \\ -6 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 8 \\ -5 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 6x_1+9x_2 \\ -3x_1-6x_2 & 3x_1 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 8 \\ -5 & 1 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} 6x_1+9x_2 = 8 \\ -3x_1-6x_2 = -5 \\ 3x_1 = 1. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 6 & 9 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 & -5 \\ 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 6 & 9 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 & -5 \\ 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+\left(\dfrac1 2\right)R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+\left(-\dfrac1 2\right)R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 6 & 9 & 8 \\ 0 & -\dfrac 3 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -\dfrac 9 2 & -3 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} 6x_1+9x_2 = 8 \\ -\dfrac 3 2x_2 = -1\\ -\dfrac 9 2x_2= -3. \end{cases} \] From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =\dfrac 2 3.$ From the first equation, we get \begin{align*} 6x_1 + 9\cdot \dfrac 2 3 &= 8 \\[3pt] 6x_1 &= 2 \\[3pt] x_1&= \dfrac 1 3. \end{align*}

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac 1 3 \\ \dfrac 2 3 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = \dfrac1 3 + \dfrac 2 3=1.$

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 7 \\ -5 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} -2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 7 \\ -5 & 0 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 2x_1 & 7x_1+3x_2 \\ -5x_1-x_2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1 = -2 \\ 7x_1+3x_2 = -1 \\ -5x_1-x_2 = 3. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 7 & 3 & -1 \\ -5 & -1 & 3 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 7 & 3 & -1 \\ -5 & -1 & 3 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+\left(-\dfrac72\right)R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+\dfrac 5 2R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} 2x_1 = -2 \\ 3x_2 = 6\\ -x_2= -2. \end{cases} \] From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =2.$ From the first equation, we get $x_1=-1.$

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = -1+2=1.$

example.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector With Respect to a Given Basis in a Matrix Vector Space

question.text:
Consider the following polynomials:

\[ p_1(t)=-1-t+2t^2, \quad p_2(t)=t-t^2, \quad q(t)=3-3t. \]

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\},$ and $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2=$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t) = q(t) \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 (-1-t+2t^2)+ x_2 (t-t^2 ) &=3-3t \\[3pt] -x_1 + (-x_1+x_2)t+(2x_1-x_2)t^2 &=3-3t. \end{align*}

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} -x_1 = 3 \\ -x_1+x_2 = -3 \\ 2x_1-x_2 = 0. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+(-1)R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+2R_1 \end{array}\\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_3 :=R_3+R_2 \end{array}\\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now

\[ \begin{cases} -x_1 = 3 \\ x_2 = -6. \end{cases} \]

From the first and second equations, we get $x_1=-3$ and $x_2 =-6.$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ -6 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2=-3+(-6) = -9.$

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} 6 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -6 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1 & -x_1+x_2 \\ 0 & x_1-x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} x_1 = 6 \\ -x_1+x_2 = -2 \\ x_1-x_2 = 2. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 6 \\ -1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 6 \\ -1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+(-1)R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -4 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1 = 6\\ x_2 = 4\\ -x_2=-4. \end{cases} \] From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =4.$ From the first equation, we get $x_1 = 6.$

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = 6+4=10.$

example.title: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector With Respect to a Given Basis in a Matrix Vector Space

question.text:
Consider the following polynomials:

\[ p_1(t)=2-t, \quad p_2(t) = 3-2t^2, \quad q(t)=3t-4t^2. \]

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\},$ and $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2=$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t) = q(t) \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 (2-t)+ x_2 (3-2t^2) &=3t-4t^2 \\[3pt] (2x_1+3x_2)-x_1t-2x_2t^2 &=3t-4t^2. \end{align*}

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1+3x_2 = 0 \\ -x_1 = 3 \\ -2x_2 = -4. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \end{array} \right] & R_1 & \leftrightarrow R_2 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:=R_2+2R_1\\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now

\[ \begin{cases} -x_1= 3\\ 3x_2 = 6 \\ - 2x_2 = -4. \end{cases} \]

From the second and third equations we get $x_2 =2.$ From the first equation, we obtain $x_1=-3.$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2=-3+2 = -1.$
